corrections: Separated OCI filesystem layers from image configuration instead of claiming every Dockerfile instruction creates a filesystem layer, and qualified OverlayFS as one storage implementation.

Corrected the Kubernetes control-plane flow: components normally watch and mutate resources through the API server, etcd is not a general component event bus, and API server-to-kubelet/webhook calls do exist.

Aligned the scheduling example with the extensible scheduling framework and clarified that CSI volume topology participates through scheduling plugins while CNI normally configures networking after scheduling.
Qualified the illustrated Service packet path as one CNI/kube-proxy implementation; iptables, IPVS, nftables and eBPF data planes can differ.
Removed the fictional fixed three-minute HPA scale-up cooldown. The default scale-up stabilization window is zero and scale-down is 300 seconds; both behavior and controller timing are configurable.
Added Immediate versus WaitForFirstConsumer storage provisioning boundaries and qualified CSI expansion, remount, availability and persistence behavior by driver and backend.
Clarified that Argo CD drift correction requires automated sync/self-heal configuration and that Deployment rolling updates do not alone guarantee uninterrupted service.
Updated service-mesh scope for Istio sidecar and ambient modes and removed the misleading fixed HALF-OPEN analogy for Envoy outlier detection.
Separated the Operator pattern from application-specific guarantees such as replica-first upgrades, zero downtime and zero data loss.
Qualified Serverless scale-to-zero, cold starts, billing and delivery semantics as provider- and trigger-specific.
Clarified Helm --atomic rollback limits and that Kubernetes Secret storage is not automatically encrypted at rest.

relationSuggestions.reason: Container image/config semantics are foundational to Kubernetes workload execution, while Kubernetes is not tied to Docker Engine.
The scheduler and binding cycle are part of Kubernetes workload reconciliation.
Kubernetes networking APIs rely on replaceable CNI and Service data-plane implementations.
PV/PVC/StorageClass and CSI integrate persistence into Kubernetes scheduling and node operation.
HPA changes desired replicas; the scheduler subsequently places newly created Pods.
GitOps reconcilers can render Helm charts, but Helm and GitOps have distinct state and reconciliation semantics.
Operators extend the Kubernetes API with custom resources and controllers.
Service meshes commonly integrate with Kubernetes but add an independent traffic data plane and policy layer.
